summary: Reject speculative decoding before model loading when either resolved target-model attention backend is torch_native, with coverage for the reported NGRAM combination, split backends, and valid controls.

tests.what_was_measured: The actual attention compatibility hook accepted NGRAM with combined, prefill-only, and decode-only torch_native backends; the new rejection assertions failed.
Four regression tests and two split-backend subtests passed: unsupported configurations reject early, while both valid boundary configurations remain accepted.
228 tests and 46 subtests passed; two unrelated context-parallel tests failed because HIP prefill CP is deprecated on the prepared ROCm platform.
Changed Python source and regression test compile successfully.
No whitespace errors in the patch.

gpu_execution.evidence: No inference kernel was needed or run for this pre-model-load argument validation. evidence/gpu-inventory.txt records the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 only.

remaining_limitations: No full server warmup was run because no production model weights were available; the failing-before regression proves the actual prepared validation hook accepted the unsupported configuration, not the later GPU traceback.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only and was not used to claim Qwen, NVIDIA, semantic, or distributed behavior.
The full server-args test file has two unrelated ROCm context-parallel expectation failures documented in evidence/test-server-args.txt.
The prepared environment does not contain the pre-commit executable; evidence/pre-commit.txt records that limitation.
